subject: business-studies
title: The BCG Matrix
welcome_lead: Stars, Cows, Question Marks, Dogs - a portfolio in four boxes.
meta_desc: A-Level BCG: four quadrants of the Boston matrix.
final_note: Use BCG to balance cash flow today against growth tomorrow.

concepts.def: High share, high growth - invest to defend leadership.
High share, low growth - milk for cash.
Low share, high growth - invest or divest.
Low share, low growth - usually divest.
Firm's share divided by largest rival's share.
Annual percentage growth in market sales.

walkthroughs.body_html: Plot each product on relative market share (horizontal, log scale) and market growth (vertical). The four quadrants suggest the cash position and strategy for each product.
Cash cows fund stars and question marks. Dogs leak cash. Question marks need decisive action - back the winners, drop the rest.
BCG assumes share drives cost via experience curves. In differentiated markets a niche dog can be very profitable. BCG is a portfolio aid, not a destiny.
